title: CCX / Workers & Queues
description: ccx-state-worker queues, task timing and state updates, plus ccx-notify-worker notifications.

panels.title: Max queue length now
panels.description: Largest current work-queue length across all state-worker queues in the selected environments.

panels.title: Tasks run / s
panels.description: Rate of state-worker work items processed (worker_time_seconds count).

panels.title: State-update errors (range)
panels.description: State-update executions that ended with status=error over the selected time range (executions_count, a per-pod counter that restarts at 0 with the pod). The error series only appears after the first failure, so 0 is shown when the worker ran without errors; no data means no state worker was scraped.

panels.title: Notification send error % (range)
panels.description: Share of outgoing notifications rejected by the outgoing service over the selected range; 0 when no errors were ever recorded (the error counter only appears after the first failure).

panels.title: Queue length by queue
panels.description: Current work-queue length per environment and queue name (stores, users); a growing line means the worker is falling behind. Shows the 10 series with the highest peak in the selected time range.

panels.title: Worker wakes by path
panels.description: Rate of work items scheduled on the state worker, by queue name and trigger (poll counts one item per datastore per poll cycle; cmon_job, cmon_hosts, ccx_job, spec_change and alert count one per event). Only the stores queue is instrumented. Shows the 10 series with the highest peak in the selected time range.

panels.title: Average task duration
panels.description: Mean time to run one work item per queue (worker_time_seconds is a summary without quantiles, so sum/count is used). Shows the 10 series with the highest peak in the selected time range.

targets.expr: topk_max(10, sum by (kubernetes_namespace, name) (rate(worker_time_seconds_sum{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (kubernetes_namespace, name) (rate(worker_time_seconds_count{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9))

panels.title: Tasks processed / s
panels.description: Rate of work items run per queue (worker_time_seconds count). Shows the 10 series with the highest peak in the selected time range.

panels.title: Item re-visit interval p50 / p90
panels.description: How long before a work item is seen again (worker_interval_seconds histogram, buckets 0.1s-600s, so quantiles are coarse).

panels.title: Item re-visit interval distribution
panels.description: Distribution of the time between sightings of the same work item, from the worker_interval_seconds histogram buckets.

panels.title: State update latency (avg) by operation
panels.description: Average duration of one state-update run per operation (state_update_latency summary, observed in milliseconds; sum/count).

panels.title: Executions by operation and status
panels.description: Rate of state-update executions per operation, split into success and error (executions_count).

panels.title: Executions per operation (range)
panels.description: Success and error counts and error ratio per state-update operation over the selected time range.

targets.expr: (sum by (operation) (increase(executions_count{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment", status="error"}[$__range])) or (0 * sum by (operation) (increase(executions_count{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"}[$__range])))) / clamp_min(sum by (operation) (increase(executions_count{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"}[$__range])), 1)

panels.title: Notifications received
panels.description: Incoming notification requests per destination (notify_recv_count). Shows the 10 series with the highest peak in the selected time range.

panels.title: Notifications sent / failed
panels.description: Outgoing messages per destination and medium (notify_send_count) and rejected sends (notify_send_error_count, only present after a first failure).

panels.title: Send error %
panels.description: Share of notification sends rejected by the outgoing service; empty means no send error has ever been recorded.

targets.expr: sum by (dest, medium) (rate(notify_send_error_count{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (dest, medium) (rate(notify_send_count{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (dest, medium) (rate(notify_send_error_count{kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.title: Datastore job queue length by type
panels.description: Number of waiting datastore jobs per job type (datastores_job_queue_length). Comes from the ccx-stores exporter (datastores/exporter), which is not scraped on this install, so the panel is empty here.

panels.title: Repairs by datastore
panels.description: Repair jobs in any state and failed repairs per datastore (datastores_repairs_total / datastores_repairs_failed). Comes from the ccx-stores exporter (datastores/exporter), which is not scraped on this install, so the panel is empty here.

panels.title: Failed repairs
panels.description: Failed repair jobs over time per environment (datastores_repairs_failed). Comes from the ccx-stores exporter (datastores/exporter), which is not scraped on this install, so the panel is empty here.

panels.title: DB connection pools
panels.description: Per environment, service and database: connections in use now on the busiest pod, the per-pod pool limit (go_sql_max_open_connections; each pod has its own pool), and how often and how long requests waited for a free connection over the dashboard range (summed over all pods). Most CCX services cap the pool at 2 connections per pod, so waits show up here first under load. A limit of 0 means unlimited. (runtime-pools)

targets.expr: max by (kubernetes_namespace, app, db_name) (go_sql_in_use_connections{job="kubernetes-pods", app=~"ccx-.*", kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"})
max by (kubernetes_namespace, app, db_name) (go_sql_max_open_connections{job="kubernetes-pods", app=~"ccx-.*", kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"})

panels.title: DB pool usage
panels.description: Connections in use as a share of the pool limit, computed per pod (each pod has its own pool) and showing the busiest pod per service and database across the selected environments. 100% means every further query on that pod waits. Pools with no limit (0) are left out. (runtime-pools)

targets.expr: max by (app, db_name) (go_sql_in_use_connections{job="kubernetes-pods", app=~"ccx-.*", kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"} / (go_sql_max_open_connections{job="kubernetes-pods", app=~"ccx-.*", kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"} > 0))

panels.title: DB pool waits
panels.description: Requests per second that had to wait for a free DB connection, summed over all pods of a service in the selected environments. See "Average DB pool wait" for how long they waited. (runtime-pools)

panels.title: Average DB pool wait
panels.description: Average time a request waited for a free DB connection, per service. Gaps mean no waits in that interval. (runtime-pools)

panels.title: Memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident memory per service, summed over all its pods in the selected environments. A steady climb that never drops points to a leak. (runtime-pools)

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines per service (highest single pod across the selected environments). Unbounded growth usually means leaked goroutines or stuck calls. (runtime-pools)

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU cores used per service, summed over all its pods in the selected environments (1 = one full core). (runtime-pools)

panels.title: GC pause (average)
panels.description: Average garbage-collection pause per service. (runtime-pools)

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Open file descriptors as a share of the process limit (highest pod per service). (runtime-pools)

targets.expr: max by (app) (process_open_fds{job="kubernetes-pods", app=~"ccx-.*", kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"} / (process_max_fds{job="kubernetes-pods", app=~"ccx-.*", kubernetes_namespace=~"$environment"} > 0))
